title: Ultrafine-grained/nanolaminate heterostructure enables exceptionally long Lüders-type stress plateau in the tensile of a high strength medium Mn steel
abstract: In general, a relatively short stress plateau followed by long and steady stress increase stage is observed on the tensile engineering stress-strain curve in cold rolled and annealed ultrafine-grained medium Mn transformation-induced plasticity (TRIP) steels, which is associated with strain-induced martensitic transformation (SIMT) of γ → α’, and stress-assisted martensitic transformation (SAMT), respectively. By contrast, this study obtained large ductility solely by an exceptionally long stress plateau up to true strain of 0.385 (47 % in elongation) in high strength (yield strength, 1230 MPa) 0.2C-8Mn-0.2Nb steel by constructing ultrafine-grained/nanolaminate ferrite and austenite heterostructure via a strategy of heterogeneous microstructure heredity. Notably, large ductility was obtained in the absence of SAMT. It was clarified that such heterostructure deformed throughout the tensile process via localized Lüders bands propagation involving multiple SIMT (γ → α’, γ → ε → α’ and γ → ε) rather than SAMT. Sequential activation of multiple discontinuous SIMT in ultrafine-grained/nanolaminate austenite sustained stable Lüders band propagation and enabled exceptionally long stress plateau. γ morphology not only affects its mechanical stability but also the SIMT mode: both γ → α’ and γ → ε → α’ take place in the ultrafine-grained austenite while stacking faults-assisted γ → ε occurs in the nanolaminate austenite with higher mechanical stability. The deformation mechanism was also demonstrated theoretically using the thermodynamics model of martensitic transformation. This work confirms that high tensile plasticity can still be obtained even without SAMT by utilizing multiple SIMT to sustain the stable propagation of localized Lüders band.
